ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a mass spectrum fragment of neon, with the vertical axis labeled Percent, and 20, 21, 22 near the mass numbers on the horizontal axis. The spectral line at mass 20 is the highest, about 90%; at mass 21 there is only a very small spectral line, about 1%; at mass 22 there is a smaller but obvious spectral line, about 9%. Reasoning: Taking the spectral line heights as relative abundances, the average mass can be calculated using a weighted average: (20×90 + 21×1 + 22×9) / (90+1+9) = (1800+21+198)/100 = 20.19. Since reading the graph is an estimate, the result is about 20.2 to 20.3, so it can be estimated as 20.3.

method.method_draft: First describe the spectrum: the tallest line is at mass 20 and reaches about 90%, a very small line is at mass 21, and a smaller but visible line is at mass 22 around 9%. planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct quantitative route: read isotope masses and relative heights from the spectrum and compute the weighted mean. With only one visual data display, this is the main genuinely distinct solution method.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the mass spectrum to identify the peaks at approximately mass 20, 21, and 22. Estimate their relative heights from the percent axis: about 90% for mass 20, about 1% for mass 21, and about 9% for mass 22.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to know the element is neon and that each line height should be interpreted as the relative amount of atoms of that mass.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that average atomic mass is the weighted average of isotope masses, with spectrum line heights representing relative abundances: average = sum(mass × percent abundance) / total percent.
